transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-17 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Alex Monroe (Redwood AE); Priya Patel (Redwood SE); Lena Ortiz (Citrine Head of ML); Markus Lee (Citrine Platform Eng); Sonia Patel (Citrine PM)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda: recap last week's perf numbers, finalize canary and cutover plan, monitoring and runbook ownership, and agree next steps.
[00:18] Lena (Citrine): Yep, thanks Alex. We had a quick internal sync earlier. We're primarily worried about latency tail and cost as we scale beyond 200 concurrent users for the pilot.
[00:30] Priya (Redwood): Good. We ran the extended throughput tests on Thursday - summary's in the sheet you have, but in short the dedicated config hits our 95th perc SLO around 220ms for 512-token avg prompt, with batching enabled. There are a couple of spikes during long KV cache warmup.
[00:48] Markus (Citrine): Sorry can you say KV cache? I think the notes had "kay vee cache" spelled out funny in the doc.
[00:54] Priya: Yeah, that's the key-value cache for the attention state. Warmup issues are expected right after deploy, that's why canary phases matter.
[01:05] Sonia (Citrine): On the cutover, we have two windows: a 2-hour rehearsal and then a 1am UTC final cutover the weekend after. We want to avoid impacting production EMR jobs - so we need a rollback that can be triggered in under 10 minutes.
[01:22] Alex: Okay. I propose the following canary: 5% traffic for 1 hour, monitor latency P50/P95, error rate, and model-quality drift (we'll run sampling). If stable, 25% for 2 hours, then 100% during final window. We also recommend a traffic mirror to staging for shadow testing.
[01:41] Lena: Sampling for quality - how do you recommend we measure that? We have a set of 500 prompts and expected outputs but it's not exhaustive.
[01:50] Priya: We suggest two things: 1) baseline BLEU-ish or embedding-similarity checks on sampled outputs vs golden set; 2) manual spot checks from your QA team on a small stratified sample for hallucinations or safety flags. We'll attach the eval harness.
[02:08] Markus: For monitoring, what dashboards and alerts should we expect? We use Grafana and Datadog for infra metrics.
[02:16] Priya: We'll provide Grafana dashboard JSON and suggested Datadog alerts. Key metrics: request latency (P50/P95/P99), token throughput, GPU utilization, queue depth, error rate by route, and model-quality regression signals (embedding drift or key metric drop). Alerts: P95 > 400ms for 5m, error rate > 1% sustained, and model-quality drop relative to baseline > 8%.
[02:43] Sonia: Model-quality alerts are tricky - false positives could trigger rollbacks. Can we set an initial "informational" alert tier?
[02:50] Alex: Absolutely. We usually start with informational or pager-suppressed alerts for quality signals during canary, then escalate on the final cutover. Rollback policy should be measured-based not finger-pointing.
[03:03] Lena: For rollback, do you support automatic fallback to hosted variants? For example, in our Dedicated pool if there's an issue, can we drain to a smaller hosted model or previous model version?
[03:13] Alex: Yes. We have automatic fallback: policy-based routing can shift traffic to a verified hosted variant or previous stable model version. We'll include config samples.
[03:22] Markus: Network and security: we need to ensure audit logs and KMS integration are in place for Private. Is that in scope for this pilot?
[03:30] Priya: For this POC you've been on Dedicated but with private networking. We can enable KMS for at-rest keys and forward audit logs to your SIEM. We'll share the doc with required IAM roles and VPC peering steps.
[03:44] Sonia: About runbooks - we need step-by-step playbooks. Who owns which steps during rehearsal?
[03:50] Alex: Good callout. We recommend split ownership: Citrine owns staging verification and smoke tests; Redwood owns canary rollout orchestration and automatic traffic shift. We'll write a runbook with explicit owners per step.
[04:03] Priya: Template we use: prereq checks, canary deploy command lines, smoke tests (synthetic and sample queries), monitoring thresholds, rollback steps, and post-mortem checklist.
[04:16] Lena: For smoke tests, we need test data - we don't want PHI in staging. Markus will seed synthetic data.
[04:24] Markus: Yup, we'll seed synthetic but realistic datasets. We'll also enable traffic mirroring so you can observe live distribution without impacting production.
[04:32] Alex: On the canary length: Lily from infra suggested we might need longer than 1 hour for cold-start heavy workloads. Recommendation: 1 hour at 5% plus 3-hour 25% for the more conservative path. Sonia, does that impact your stakeholder schedule?
[04:47] Sonia: It pushes the schedule a bit but is safer. I'm fine with the conservative approach if the team can commit to the rehearsal weekend.
[04:55] [05:00] Alex: Great. Next, A/B testing vs progressive ramp: do you want to run A/B for model-variants or purely progressive traffic ramp for the same config?
[05:10] Lena: We want to validate a quantized variant (lower cost) against the full fp16 model - so A/B for quality comparison and progressive for rollouts.
[05:18] Priya: Perfect. Our platform supports route-based A/B with split percentages and automated quality sampling. We'll set up experiment IDs so we can attribute results.
[05:27] Markus: Any offline benchmarks we should run before canary? We ran perf tests but saw some variance on token lengths > 1024.
[05:36] Priya: Run the long-sequence synthetic suite; we'll provide the exact commands. Also include warmup traffic (prefix caching) to avoid initial P99 spikes.
[05:46] Lena: Who's on the cutover call? We should list exact people and escalation contacts.
[05:52] Alex: Suggested list: Alex (Redwood AE) - coordination; Priya (SE) - deploy ops; Markus (Platform) - network/VPC; Lena (ML) - quality owner; Sonia (PM) - stakeholder. We'll add your on-call infra person and our SRE.
[06:08] Sonia: Ok. For compliance, we need SOC2 evidence on log retention and role-based access.
[06:14] Priya: We'll include the SOC2 summary and our audit log retention config. For POC we can show screenshots and configuration pointers; enterprise package includes full audit exports.
[06:25] Markus: A nit: the demo last week mentioned "smart routing" and automatic fallback - is it per-request or at the session level?
[06:32] Alex: It's per-request routing with sticky sessions optionally. For chat sessions you can keep KV cache affinity to same instance to preserve context, but fallback can be at request level if the policy says degrade to hosted.
[06:44] Lena: Any concerns about data residency for EU users? We have a handful of EU customers in pilot.
[06:51] Priya: We can pin region routing and ensure model inference happens in the EU region. We'll include the geo-routing policy sample.
[06:58] Alex: Alright let's walk through the proposed timeline - I'll share this in the notes after the call. Proposed: 2026-06-22 staging fully ready; 2026-06-24 canary rehearsal (internal); 2026-06-29 cutover rehearsal with stakeholders; 2026-06-30 final go-live window.
[07:18] Sonia: Sounds tight but doable. Can we get the runbook and dashboards by Friday?
[07:24] Priya: Yes, I'll send runbook template and dashboard JSON by Friday (2026-06-19).
[07:29] Alex: I'll send the rollout checklist and canary playbook tomorrow (2026-06-18). I'll also attach the fallback config samples for draining and rollback.
[07:38] Lena: For quality validation during canary, can Redwood host the sampling harness or do we need to run it locally?
[07:46] Priya: We can host the harness and push a small sampling job that posts results to your S3. For PHI constraints you can run the quality harness in your environment; we can provide the runner.
[07:57] Markus: One more thing - cost monitoring and alerting. We need to ensure unit cost per 1k tokens doesn't spike during canary.
[08:05] Alex: We'll include token-cost metrics and set a cost alert: >20% deviation from baseline triggers an informational alert during canary, and an escalated alert for >40% deviation.
[08:17] Sonia: That helps. Let's recap next steps.
[08:20] Alex: Recap: Redwood to send rollout checklist and canary playbook (Alex) by 6/18; SE to send runbook and dashboards (Priya) by 6/19; Citrine to provision staging VPC and seed synthetic data (Markus) by 6/22; Sonia to confirm stakeholder availability by 6/20. Schedule rehearsal dates as discussed.
[08:40] Lena: Great, we'll aim to have the staging mirrors up early next week.
[08:45] Alex: Any other questions?
[08:47] Sonia: Not from me. Thanks everyone.
[08:50] Alex: Thanks - we'll follow up in email with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the rehearsals.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., "kay vee cache" for KV cache, "quan-tize-ation" mis-heard), some speaker overlaps and filler words removed for readability.

References mentioned: shared sheet with perf numbers (link: https://redwood.share/perf-sheet), runbook template (to be sent), Grafana dashboard JSON (to be attached), SOC2 summary doc (link to be shared).
